what: A saw wave whose slope and notch you can bend, from bright and full to hollow.
how: Instead of a plain saw wave, VARISAW has two controls over its outline. SHAPE bends the wave's slope (the ramp), and NOTCH carves a notch in it. Together they sweep from a bright buzzy saw to a more hollow, pulse-like tone.

ins.pitch: Pitch in octaves (1 volt per octave, 0 is middle C). Patch KEYS' pitch here.
ins.shape: A control signal that adds to SHAPE (each 1.0 adds 0.5). Patch an LFO or ENV for a moving tone.

knobs.shape: The slope of the wave, 0 to 1. Moves the tone between a plain ramp and a more bent wave.
knobs.notch: The depth of the notch cut into the wave, 0 to 1. Changes the hollowness of the tone.
knobs.tune: Shifts the pitch in semitones, -24 to 24 (two octaves down to two up), added to the pitch input.

try: Patch KEYS' pitch into VARISAW's pitch, VARISAW's out into a VCA (with an ENV) and then OUT. Hold a note and move SHAPE and NOTCH to hear the colour change.
